symbols.name: packed ring element
symbols.meaning: A ring element with integer coefficients $f_j$, the first of the two elements being packed.
symbols.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ be ring elements with integer coefficients $f_j$ and $g_j$.

symbols.name: second ring element
symbols.meaning: A ring element with integer coefficients $g_j$, the second of the two elements being packed.
symbols.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ be ring elements with integer coefficients $f_j$ and $g_j$.

symbols.name: coefficient bound
symbols.meaning: A bound on the absolute value of every coefficient of f and g.
symbols.quote: Let $M$ be a bound on the absolute value of every such coefficient.

symbols.name: coefficient position
symbols.meaning: An index running over the r coefficient positions of f and g, from 0 to r-1.
symbols.quote: The index $j$ runs over the $r$ coefficient positions, $0 \le j < r$.

symbols.name: product position
symbols.meaning: An index over the coefficient positions of the unreduced product w.
symbols.quote: Here $k$ also indexes coefficient positions, not transform positions.

symbols.name: packing base
symbols.meaning: A power of two, larger than 2rM^2, at which the coefficient lists are evaluated.
symbols.quote: Fix a power of two $B$ with $B > 2rM^2$, and call $B$ the packing base.

symbols.name: packed integer of f
symbols.meaning: The integer obtained by evaluating f at B.
symbols.quote: The packed integer of $f$ is $F = \sum_j f_j B^j$, which may be negative because the digits are signed.

symbols.name: packed integer of g
symbols.meaning: The integer obtained by evaluating g at B.
symbols.quote: Packing $g$ the same way gives the packed integer $G = \sum_j g_j B^j$.

symbols.name: unreduced product
symbols.meaning: The product fg before reduction modulo y^r+1, whose coefficients are w_k.
symbols.quote: Let $w = fg$ be the unreduced product, that is, before reduction modulo $y^r+1$, with coefficients $w_k = \sum_j f_j g_{k-j}$, where $k$ is the power of $y$ and the sum runs over $0 \le k-j < r$.

relations.quote: Signed Kronecker packing maps each element of [Polynomial ring modulo yʳ + 1](polynomial-ring-y.md) to a single integer, by evaluating it at a large power of two.
Signed Kronecker packing is an instance of [Multiplication as convolution of digits](convolution-reduction.md): the coefficients act as digits and the evaluation point as the radix.
